items.title: WordPress Database Connection Error: Safe First Checks
items.demandEvidence: Research-backed editorial queue topic from official WordPress troubleshooting documentation. Search demand, impressions, and community volume have not been measured for this brief.
items.whyWeCanWin: Focus the guide on distinguishing configuration issues from host/database availability problems, preserving sensitive credentials, and knowing when to contact the host. This narrower troubleshooting intent complements the existing general site-down and plugin-conflict checklists.
outline: What the database-connection error indicates and what it does not diagnose by itself
Record the exact message, affected URLs, recent changes, and provider alerts before changing files
Check whether the host reports a database or resource issue before editing configuration
Protect credentials and backups; avoid publishing or copying wp-config.php contents
When to involve the hosting provider or a WordPress technician

items.title: Google URL Inspection: What a Website Owner Can Check
items.demandEvidence: Research-backed editorial queue topic using current Google Search Central documentation. No Search Console performance data or search-volume estimate is attached.
items.whyWeCanWin: Explain how to use an official Google tool to investigate one URL and set realistic expectations about indexing requests. Keep crawling, indexing, and ranking as separate ideas and avoid guaranteeing inclusion or timing.

items.title: Local Business Website Details: Keep Location Information Clear
items.demandEvidence: Research-backed editorial queue topic based on Google Search Central's public documentation. No local ranking factor, search volume, or performance result is claimed.
items.whyWeCanWin: Help a service business decide what location and coverage information belongs on its site, and distinguish real service areas from thin location pages. Ground structured-data advice in Google's documentation and avoid claiming that markup guarantees enhanced search results.
outline: State the business name and contact details consistently with the real organization
Describe actual coverage plainly instead of generating near-duplicate neighborhood pages
Keep structured data aligned with information visible on the page
What LocalBusiness markup can describe and what it cannot guarantee
Review the service-page structure and contact path before launch
